text:
Avery: Heads-up — I sketched a proposal for cost-aware routing that automatically falls back to cheaper model variants for lower tiers and region-specific capacity limits. Wanted engineering + billing + product eyes.

Kai: +1 to the idea. Can you paste the suggested routing config?

Avery: Sure — rough draft below. Key idea: per-customer-tier 'max_cost_per_request' and a ranked list of compatible variants. If primary variant is unhealthy or capacity-constrained, route to the next cheaper compatible one.

Avery: ```
route_policy: 
  - tier: free
    max_cost_per_request: 0.0015  # $/request budget cap
    variants: ["redwood-compact-8q", "redwood-int8-12b"]
    latency_slo_ms: 1200
  - tier: pro
    max_cost_per_request: 0.01
    variants: ["redwood-8b-quant", "redwood-14b-int8"]
    latency_slo_ms: 600
  - tier: enterprise
    variants: ["redwood-70b-fp16"]
    latency_slo_ms: 200
```

Mina: That config looks reasonable but we need telemetry hooks. We should emit per-request decision_reason and cost_estimate to trace so Console can show why a request hit variant X vs fallback Y.

Priya: +telemetry. Also need a knob for devs to opt-out per-route (some apps require specific model family). Add `force_model_family` flag at route level.

Luis: Two implementation questions: 1) where do we enforce cost cap — at the routing layer before claim, or post-inference as a billing adjustment? 2) what about token-budgeting for streaming requests?

Avery: My preference: enforce pre-claim check using a cheap cost estimator (based on expected tokens from prompt metadata and average completion tokens) so we avoid spinning up GPUs for requests that exceed cap. For streaming, do a rolling budget — if estimate crosses cap mid-stream, auto-fallback to cheaper variant or terminate with a structured error.

Nora: That pre-claim estimator will need regular calibration per-customer prompt patterns. We should surface per-route average token usage in Console and have an auto-suggest to relax caps for customers that keep hitting them.

billing-bot: FYI — any enforcement that drops or downgrades service for paid customers will change invoices. We need a clear mapping: if we fallback to a cheaper model automatically, charge the cheaper model price. If we fail the request due to cap, show a clear billing event code.

Priya: Agreed. For UX: Console should show a per-customer 'routing budget' widget with historical decisions, percent of traffic downgraded, and cost-savings estimate. Also allow enabling a "grace quota" that uses bursts of higher-cost variants for a short window.

Kai: On the infra side, fallback must be fast. Suggest we implement variant selection as part of the request admission path — check health + estimated cost + tier policy in one critical path. Keep decision logic small and cache policy lookups.

Luis: Also watch out for cascading fallbacks causing heavier variants to get overloaded. We need capacity-aware scoring: prefer fallbacks that actually have capacity in region. If none, try cross-region with latency penalty if customer's policy allows it.

Avery: Yes — scoring should be multi-dimensional: cost_score, latency_penalty, region_affinity, capacity_score. We'll compute a composite score and pick highest. Default tie-breaker: cheapest within SLO.

Mina: For telemetry, add these fields: decision_reason (primary|fallback|capacity|cost_cap), chosen_variant, estimated_cost, actual_cost, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms. Keep them in tracing and a separate per-route aggregation feed for Console.

Nora: For the rollout: ops team, can we try this behind a feature flag for 5% of free tier traffic in us-west first and monitor rollback triggers?

deploy-bot: deployment queued: feature-flag 'tiered-cost-routing' -> canary 5% on us-west (eng-platform) 

Luis: Rollout triggers: >2x error rate, >15% latency regression for pro, or >30% of free-tier requests failing pre-claim. Also monitor billing mismatch events.

Priya: Need product acceptance criteria too: Console surfaces downgraded rate, per-request decision log, and an override toggle per customer.

Avery: One more internal API debate — should policy be defined in Platform Config service (central) or be part of Account service (per-customer)? Central makes it easier to reason about global defaults, per-customer overrides in Account would be lower-latency for admission checks. Thoughts?

Kai: I'd keep the policy in a central store but use a local hot-cache populated with per-customer overrides. That gives single source of truth and fast reads. We'll need an efficient invalidation stream.

Mina: +1. We can piggyback on existing config-change stream (Kafka) and add a small merkle-based version to avoid sending full blobs.

billing-bot: Also add `billing_policy_version` in trace so we can reconcile charge decisions later.

Nora: For the Console UX when a customer gets downgraded, how do we explain? Prefer a short message: "Your request used a cost-optimized model variant because your plan's per-request budget was reached. Upgrade to Pro for higher-fidelity models." Link to docs.

Priya: We'll mock the widget: include chart, recent decisions, toggle for grace quota, and a button to request temporary override.

Avery: OK next steps I propose:
1) Eng: prototype admission-layer estimator + scoring in a canary branch (Kai, Luis)
2) ML infra: add capacity signals + variant pricing table (Mina)
3) Billing: define billing contract for fallback and cap failures (billing team)
4) Product/Console: mockups & acceptance (Priya, Nora)
5) Launch canary 5% free tier us-west, monitor telemetry and rollback triggers (deploy-bot will run)

Kai: Assigning tasks in linear now. I'll start a PR with the routing decision proto and a lightweight estimator function.

Mina: I'll add the telemetry schema and wire the estimated_cost/actual_cost fields.

Luis: I'll draft the capacity-aware scoring algorithm and a small simulation to validate non-cascading behavior.

Avery: Thanks all. If nobody objects, I'll start the feature flag and schedule the canary for tomorrow morning.

Priya: No objections from product. :thumbsup:

Nora: Sounds good. Please include a short blurb for CS so they can prep customer comms if we see a lot of downgrade requests.

Kai: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/routing/pulls/452 — includes proto + basic estimator.

Mina: Telemetry schema PR: https://git.internal/redwood/telemetry/pulls/128

Avery: Will post results of the canary in this thread.

deploy-bot: canary started: tiered-cost-routing -> 5% us-west at 2024-11-02T09:15:23Z

Avery: Canary initial metrics after 15m: downgraded_rate_free=4.8%, avg_estimated_saving_per_request=$0.0011, no increase in pro latency. Monitoring logging for estimator accuracy.

Luis: Simulation matches early canary: cascading fallback probability <0.5% with current capacity weights.

Mina: Logged a small estimator bias on long prompts, adjusting calibration.

Priya: Great — keep Console rollout on hold until we have a full hour of stable metrics.

Avery: Will report back. Thanks team!
